summary: Olivia Chow's Instagram record presents housing affordability as a central priority, framing Toronto as facing an affordability and homelessness crisis after a decade of inaction (CspF_1zANJZ, Cr_i5mPJMRP). Chow advocates the City acting as a public developer, pledging 25,000 rent-controlled homes over 8 years on city-owned land under a "City Homes Plan" (Cr_Yy69ga2k, Cr_i5mPJMRP, CtHTQmxAsFH). Chow proposes $100M/year to prevent renovictions, 1,000–3,000 rent supplements, and a Toronto Renters Action Committee (CtPRf7mgQPR, CsHejOWP0rO, CtkGd5mPLWL). Chow supports community land trusts, co-op housing, culturally responsive housing, and stronger tenant protections against renovictions, demovictions, and bad landlords (CtPRf7mgQPR, Cujn8P6utFZ, CtIQZymtA3s, uY0e37utHo). Earlier 2014 posts similarly back community housing, tenant rights, and fighting federal co-op funding cuts (uJqN2uOtLA, rpM-RoutEa, qCNKA4utO3).

key_positions.stance: Supports the City of Toronto acting as a public developer to build affordable housing, rather than relying on private developers alone.
Supports building 25,000 new rent-controlled homes on city-owned land.
Supports community land trusts and community ownership models to keep homes affordable and prevent displacement.
Supports stronger renter protections, including preventing renovictions, demovictions, above-guideline increases, and protecting affordable rentals.
Supports rent supplements to help people secure permanent housing.
Supports preserving existing affordable housing, including co-op housing.
Supports affordable, supportive, and culturally responsive housing for diverse populations including seniors and survivors of gender-based violence.
Frames housing affordability and homelessness as an urgent crisis requiring city action after a decade of inaction.

key_actions.action: Announced the City Homes Plan to build 25,000 rent-controlled homes over 8 years on city-owned land.
Released a Secure Affordable Homes / renter protection plan to fund proven measures protecting renters.
Pledged $100M/year to prevent renovictions and secure affordable homes.
Pledged 1,000 new rent supplements with a request to provincial/federal governments to match for 2,000 more.
Pledged to establish a Toronto Renters Action Committee.
Met with renters affected by demovictions, renovictions, and rent increases.
Met with United Way Greater Toronto and partners to discuss community-focused housing models like Scarborough's Golden Mile.
Announced an affordable housing plan during 2014 mayoral campaign.
Pledged to fight federal cuts to co-op housing support for 29 co-ops.
